subproblem.title: Adapted frame of a nonzero functional ℓ on ℝ^{m+1}: norm-preserving ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1}, e ⟂ range ι with ℓ(e) = 1, and p with ι(p(u)) + ℓ(u)e = u
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and let ℓ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ be a nonzero continuous linear functional (ℝ^k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with the Euclidean inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|). Then there are continuous linear maps ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} and p : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^m and a vector e ∈ ℝ^{m+1} such that ℓ(e) = 1, |ι(v)| = |v| and ⟨ι(v), e⟩ = 0 for every v ∈ ℝ^m, and ι(p(u)) + ℓ(u)·e = u for every u ∈ ℝ^{m+1}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ℓ : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ), ℓ ≠ 0 → ∃ (ι : Eucl m →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1)) (p : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] Eucl m) (e : Eucl (m + 1)), ℓ e = 1 ∧ (∀ v, ‖ι v‖ = ‖v‖) ∧ (∀ v, inner ℝ (ι v) e = 0) ∧ ∀ u, ι (p u) + ℓ u • e = u
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (slicing_im_st_level_set_charts): "Let a ∈ ℝ^{m+1} be the gradient of ℓ := Dh(w₀) (ℓ(u) = ⟨a, u⟩, a ≠ 0) and e := a/|a|², so ℓ(e) = 1. The kernel K₀ := ker ℓ = a^⊥ has dimension m. Fix a linear isometry ι₀ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} with range K₀ (from an orthonormal basis of K₀ indexed by Fin m; ι₀ = 0 if m = 0)", together with the inverse of the linear isomorphism (v, s) ↦ ι₀v + se of Step 4. Here ℓ is an arbitrary nonzero functional and the frame is packaged as (ι, p, e).

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ (inner ℝ) and Euclidean norm |·|; B(x, r) = ball x r is the open ball; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x for a map f.

1. (Gradient vector.) ℝ^{m+1} is a finite-dimensional, hence complete, real inner product space, so by the Riesz representation theorem there is a ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with ℓ(u) = ⟨a, u⟩ for all u (Lean: a := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Eucl (m+1))).symm ℓ and InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply). If a = 0 then ℓ(u) = 0 for all u, i.e. ℓ = 0, contrary to the hypothesis; so a ≠ 0 and |a| ≠ 0.

2. (The vector e.) Put e := |a|⁻²·a. Then ℓ(e) = |a|⁻²⟨a, a⟩ = |a|⁻²|a|² = 1 (inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq).

3. (dim ker ℓ = m.) Since ℓ ≠ 0 there is u₀ with ℓ(u₀) ≠ 0 (otherwise ℓ = 0 by extensionality). Every y ∈ ℝ equals ℓ((y/ℓ(u₀))·u₀), so range ℓ = ℝ, which has dimension 1. By rank–nullity (LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker), 1 + dim ker ℓ = dim ℝ^{m+1} = m + 1 (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), hence K := ker ℓ has dimension m.

4. (An isometry from ℝ^m onto K.) K is a finite-dimensional inner product space (with the restricted inner product) of dimension m. Take an orthonormal basis of K and index it by Fin m (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ K, reindexed along finCongr : Fin (finrank ℝ K) ≃ Fin m). Its coordinate map is a linear isometric equivalence K ≃ ℝ^m (OrthonormalBasis.repr); let J : ℝ^m ≃ K be its inverse, again a linear isometric equivalence. Define the continuous linear map ι := (inclusion K ↪ ℝ^{m+1}) ∘ J. The norm of K is the restriction of the norm of ℝ^{m+1}, so |ι(v)| = |J(v)| = |v| for every v ∈ ℝ^m. (If m = 0 then K = {0} and ι = 0.)

5. (Orthogonality to e.) For v ∈ ℝ^m we have ι(v) = J(v) ∈ K = ker ℓ, so 0 = ℓ(ι(v)) = ⟨a, ι(v)⟩. Hence ⟨ι(v), e⟩ = |a|⁻²⟨ι(v), a⟩ = |a|⁻²⟨a, ι(v)⟩ = 0 (symmetry of the real inner product).

6. (The left inverse p.) For u ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, ℓ(u − ℓ(u)e) = ℓ(u) − ℓ(u)ℓ(e) = 0 by step 2, so the continuous linear map u ↦ u − ℓ(u)e (that is, id − ℓ.smulRight e) takes values in K. Let q : ℝ^{m+1} → K be its corestriction to K (ContinuousLinearMap.codRestrict), and put p := J⁻¹ ∘ q, a continuous linear map ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^m. Then ι(p(u)) = J(J⁻¹(q(u))) = q(u) = u − ℓ(u)e (LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply), i.e. ι(p(u)) + ℓ(u)e = u for every u.

7. (Conclusion.) ι, p and e satisfy ℓ(e) = 1 (step 2), |ι(v)| = |v| (step 4), ⟨ι(v), e⟩ = 0 (step 5) and ι(p(u)) + ℓ(u)e = u (step 6). ∎

Remark (not needed for the statement). Since ℓ(ι(v)) = 0 and p(ι(v) + se) = J⁻¹(ι(v)) = v, the maps (v, s) ↦ ι(v) + se and u ↦ (p(u), ℓ(u)) are mutually inverse linear isomorphisms ℝ^m × ℝ ≅ ℝ^{m+1}; this is the linear isomorphism of Step 4 of the parent proof.

  intro m ℓ hℓ
  -- Riesz vector `a` of `ℓ` (`ℓ u = ⟪a, u⟫`) and `e := ‖a‖⁻² • a`, so that `ℓ e = 1`.
  set a : Eucl (m + 1) := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Eucl (m + 1))).symm ℓ with ha
  have hℓa : ∀ u, ℓ u = inner ℝ a u := fun u => by
    rw [ha, InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply]
  have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    apply hℓ
    ext u
    simp [hℓa, h0]
  have hna : ‖a‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.2 ha0
  set e : Eucl (m + 1) := (‖a‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ • a with he
  have hℓe : ℓ e = 1 := by
    rw [hℓa, he, inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
    field_simp
  -- `K := ker ℓ` has dimension `m`: `ℓ` maps onto `ℝ`, then rank–nullity.
  set K : Submodule ℝ (Eucl (m + 1)) := LinearMap.ker ℓ.toLinearMap with hKdef
  have htop : LinearMap.range ℓ.toLinearMap = ⊤ := by
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ : ∃ u, ℓ u ≠ 0 := by
      by_contra hcon
      apply hℓ
      ext u
      by_contra hu
      exact hcon ⟨u, by simpa using hu⟩
    rw [eq_top_iff]
    rintro y -
    refine ⟨(y / ℓ u) • u, ?_⟩
    simp [hu]
  have hK : Module.finrank ℝ K = m := by
    rw [hKdef]
    have hrn := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker ℓ.toLinearMap
    rw [htop, finrank_top, Module.finrank_self, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin] at hrn
    omega
  -- A linear isometry `J : ℝ^m ≃ K` from an orthonormal basis of `K` indexed by `Fin m`;
  -- `ι := (K ↪ ℝ^{m+1}) ∘ J` and `p u := J⁻¹ (u - ℓ u • e)`.
  let J : Eucl m ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] K := ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ K).reindex (finCongr hK)).repr.symm
  let ι : Eucl m →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1) :=
    K.subtypeL.comp J.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap
  have hιK : ∀ v, ι v ∈ K := fun v => (J v).2
  have hmemK : ∀ u, u - ℓ u • e ∈ K := by
    intro u
    simp [hKdef, LinearMap.mem_ker, hℓe]
  let q : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] K :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Eucl (m + 1)) - ℓ.smulRight e).codRestrict K (by
      intro u
      simpa using hmemK u)
  let p : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] Eucl m :=
    J.symm.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap.comp q
  refine ⟨ι, p, e, hℓe, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro v
    show ‖((J v : K) : Eucl (m + 1))‖ = ‖v‖
    rw [Submodule.norm_coe, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map]
  · intro v
    have h1 : ℓ (ι v) = 0 := hιK v
    rw [hℓa] at h1
    rw [he, inner_smul_right, real_inner_comm, h1, mul_zero]
  · intro u
    show ((J (J.symm (q u)) : K) : Eucl (m + 1)) + ℓ u • e = u
    rw [LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    simp [q]
proof_key_steps: Riesz: ℓ(u) = ⟨a, u⟩ with a ≠ 0; e := |a|⁻²a satisfies ℓ(e) = 1.
range ℓ = ℝ and rank–nullity give dim ker ℓ = m.
An orthonormal basis of K = ker ℓ indexed by Fin m gives a linear isometry J : ℝ^m ≃ K; ι := (K ↪ ℝ^{m+1}) ∘ J preserves norms.
ι(v) ∈ ker ℓ = a^⊥, so ⟨ι(v), e⟩ = 0.
p(u) := J⁻¹(u − ℓ(u)e) (u − ℓ(u)e ∈ ker ℓ) gives ι(p(u)) + ℓ(u)e = u.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree on every hypothesis and conclusion. Riesz representation constructs e; surjectivity and rank–nullity give a kernel of dimension m; an orthonormal basis constructs the norm-preserving ι; and corestricting u ↦ u − ℓ(u)e constructs p with the required identity. Orthogonality and continuity are justified, including m = 0. No child or parent theorem is assumed.
